title: Context-Switch Hour Hotspots
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=rescuetime:activity
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(application) as app_count by _time
| where app_count>8
| sort - app_count
description: Finds the hours where too many different apps were active, a good proxy for mentally expensive context switching.
value: People often feel scattered before they can explain why; app diversity per hour is a surprisingly useful breadcrumb toward better focus design.
implementation: Forward RescueTime activity with application labels; review the noisiest hours and restructure notifications or batching around them.
visualization: Hourly chart of distinct active applications.
grandmaExplanation: It logs which hours had so many different apps involved that your attention was probably getting yanked around.
